design:
1. What the person sets, in one place. Settings opens on Basics; its Claude row becomes 'Claude: which to use first, and when it runs out', global (every project, every kind of call). It lists the saved credentials in order with what each costs ('1. Claude subscription: through Claude Code, your plan's limits, no money per use', '2. API key: straight to the API, money per use') and six presets, one checked, each a label and one line: A 'Subscription first, then API key' (When your subscription runs out, the work goes on with your API key by itself. It costs money; every switch is shown with its cost.); B 'Subscription first, ask before API key' (When your subscription runs out, one card asks you: use your API key, with its cost, or wait.); C 'Subscription first, then wait' (When your subscription runs out, the work waits for it. Your API key is used only for work only it can do.); D 'API key first, then subscription'; E 'API key first, ask before subscription'; F 'API key first, then wait' (the same lines with the names swapped; going on with the subscription costs no money). Under them once: 'Runs out means its usage limit, the share of your subscription Forerunner may use, your API key's monthly limit, or Anthropic refusing it.' and the optional field 'Most your API key may spend in a month: CHF [ ]' (empty: no limit of its own; the monthly cap of all spending still applies). With one credential saved the section reads 'Only your API key is saved. When it runs out, the work waits.' and keeps the stored rule for when a second one is saved. A person who never chose sees today's state named above the presets ('Not chosen yet: tasks use your subscription first; chat, planning and reviews use your API key first. When one runs out, the work waits.'). A choice that narrows what may be spent (to B, C, E or F, a lower key limit) saves at once; one that widens it (to A or D, the API key put first, a higher or no key limit) asks once ('Your API key may then be used without asking when your subscription runs out. It costs money; every switch is shown with its cost. [Use it] [Cancel]'). Each choice is one change-log row with one Undo (an Undo that widens asks the same yes). Chat can set it in words with a read-back; no agent, specialist, task check or text from a card, page or file can widen it. Stored as human.notify_prefs.credential_policy { order, whenStopped: next | ask | wait, keyMonthlyUsdMicro? } through settings.set credential_policy.

2. What 'runs out' is: four stops, each with a stop key and when it ends. Its usage limit as the provider reports it (Claude Code's 'hit your limit', the API's spend cap, spend limit or credit balance): until the reported reset, else an hour, as today. The plan-share cap (the share of the subscription Forerunner may use this month, 95% of the allowance by default): until the 1st of next month, or earlier when the allowance is raised. The API key's own monthly limit (the field above): until the 1st of next month, or when raised or cleared. A refusal (a 401 or 403 key, an expired sign-in): until a different credential is saved (the fingerprint, as today). Not stops and never a reason to switch: the monthly cap of all spending, a project's, session's or task's budget (no credential helps: subscription spend counts against them as its API-equivalent; ADR 0112's pause as today), a throttle (retried once at once), a credential not saved or turned off (the chooser's ordinary next choice). The caps check the plan-share level (as today) and a new key-monthly level before every call, so neither is ever passed mid-run.

3. What happens at a stop, by the rule. 'next': the work goes on with the next credential in the order at once, the stopped task too, from the work it kept (a repository task's work-in-progress commit and its handoff, as a budget pause keeps it); only within the chooser's group: a task never moves to a credential that cannot do it as properly (a research task whose API key ran out does not move to a subscription that cannot open pages; it waits and its row says why). When the first choice serves again the next pick uses it again; a run in progress is never re-routed. 'ask': nothing moves; the first time the credential stops while work needs it (a task run, a review, planning, the task check), one Inbox card is filed for that stop: 'Your Claude subscription reached its limit' / 'Your waiting work can go on with your API key until 15:40 (about CHF 1.20), or wait.' [Use API key] ('Goes on now on your API key until 15:40; about CHF 1.20, booked on it.') [Wait until 15:40] ('Nothing moves until then; your session goes on at 15:40.'). 'Use API key' is a grant for this stop only: while the same stop stands, the granted credential serves every kind of call; it ends by itself when the stop ends (the reset, a new credential, a raised allowance or key limit), when the person changes the policy, or with 'Stop using it' on the card's Done line. 'wait': nothing moves onto any other credential, in either direction, for any kind of call; the work whose first choice stopped waits; work whose first choice is another credential (the chooser's hard needs) runs. A wait is shown, never reminded (no notification for waiting work, D6).

4. Sessions, with D6 (the d1109-starts design). A session ends at a wait as today ('Stopped to wait for a Claude credential') with the wait entry naming it; when the wait ends the session the person started goes on (its continuation, the starts design); work waiting outside a person's session is only prepared and runs at the next Start, unless the hands-off setting is on. Under 'ask', 'Use API key' is the person's word: the continuation starts at once as a person start (by: 'person') on the granted credential; 'Wait until 15:40' keeps the continuation for the reset; an unanswered card closes itself when the stop ends ('Closed: your subscription serves again.') and the continuation goes on as under 'wait'. Under 'next' there is no session boundary: the session goes on with the other credential. No answer, setting change or reset starts a session that no Start, schedule or hands-off setting asked for.

5. Every kind of call follows the same rule. Task runs and the critic's reviews (the critic spends too): as point 3; a review that cannot be billed waits with its task (in review, no try counted, ADR 0100 point 16). Planning (the plan from a brief, Change the plan) and D7's task check: under 'ask' the same card covers them and the project page says 'Planning waits for your answer: use your API key?' [Answer]; under 'wait' the plan waits and is drafted again when the stop ends (today's wake; no task runs). Chat makes no model call while its first choice is held: under 'ask' and 'wait' the reply is one line, 'Your Claude subscription is at its limit until 15:40, so I have not answered.' with [Use API key] ('Answers this question on your API key: about CHF 0.02.'); the press answers that one question on the other credential (the card's grant also covers chat until the stop ends); commands that need no model still run; under 'next' chat answers on the other one and its footer says 'Answered on your API key (CHF 0.01): your subscription is at its limit until 15:40.'. Background jobs (the model watch, the monthly calibration) never get a card and never switch under 'ask' or 'wait': the run spends nothing, logs one line and runs at its next time.

6. A refusal follows the same rule and also tells. One refused card per refusal ('Anthropic refused your API key'), with what was refused and how to fix it (Save a new key: the setup assistant), and its notification. Under 'ask' it is the ask card (one card: the fix link and the choice); under 'next' its body says where the work goes on ('Until then your work goes on with your Claude subscription.' / '... with your API key, which costs money.'); under 'wait' 'Until then the work that needs it waits.'. A refused credential is never called again until a different one is saved: not by a switch, a grant, a continuation, a late answer, chat or a background job (one 401 per credential; nothing that could lock the account).

7. What the person sees, wherever the work is. The Start dialog and the plan card: one line under the estimate, from one function ('If your subscription runs out, you are asked before your API key is used.' / '..., the work goes on with your API key (costs money).' / '..., the work waits for it.' and the API-key-first forms); nothing with one credential. Task rows: 'Waits until 15:40 (your subscription's limit)' (today's), 'Waits until Tue 1 Dec (your subscription's share)', 'Waits until Tue 1 Dec (your API key's monthly limit)', 'Waits for your answer: use your API key?' (links the card). The project status: rule 1 'Waiting for you: use your API key?'. The session page: '"Style the page" goes on with your API key: your Claude subscription reached its limit until 15:40.', 'Your Claude subscription serves again; the next tasks use it.', and in the result 'On your API key after your subscription's limit: 2 tasks, CHF 0.83.'. The task drawer's run: 'On your API key after your subscription's limit · CHF 0.43'. Costs: a 'By credential' table (your API key in CHF; your subscription as its estimated API-equivalent, of its allowance). Under 'next' one notification per switch and session: 'Quote page goes on with your API key' / 'Your Claude subscription reached its limit until 15:40. Its waiting work is about CHF 1.20.'. Under 'wait' and 'ask' no switch, so no switch notification (the ask card's own card notification is the existing one). Times in the person's time zone, CHF only, no ids.

8. Money invariants the engine keeps. A wait or an unanswered ask moves nothing: no call on another credential for any purpose. A switch or a grant changes only which credential pays: every call still meets the run, task, session, project and month caps, the plan-share level and the key-monthly level before it is made. The card's 'Use API key' is offered only when the other credential can serve now and the caps have room for the waiting work's next call; its CHF is the waiting tasks' estimate as the Start dialog prices it, never more than the session's work budget left. A card is answered once (version-checked); a second or late answer changes nothing and gets the card's Done line; an answer that finds the stop over grants nothing ('Your subscription serves again; the work goes on there.'). Each switch is data, not only words: the run row's billing source and why it switched, a billing.switch session event, the session result's switched list with the CHF booked, and the ledger rows per credential.

9. Restart and two at once. Every mark lives on the billing source's limits and is written with the version check (updateSourceLimits): the rest, the refusal, the wait entries, asking { stopKey, requestId } (only the writer that set it files the card), grant { to, stopKey, by, at }, switchNotified { stopKey, sessionId }; the policy lives in notify_prefs; the card in the human-request store. Two stops landing together (a task run and a chat call, a run and a review) file one card, write one grant and send one notification; after a restart every wait, card, grant and continuation reads the same; no money decision is held in memory. The wake (before every scheduler tick) ends the grants and withdraws the ask cards whose stop is over, before it takes the waits.

10. Migration without changing a choice. Read at every pick, nothing rewritten: with no credential_policy stored, the order is billing_order (never chosen: today's split, tasks subscription first and every other call CALL_FALLBACK_ORDER) and the rule is mid_session_limit (use_other: next; anything else: wait). The first preset choice writes credential_policy; its Undo brings the old reading back. billing_order and mid_session_limit stay readable for old Undo rows, leave the chat model's settings tool, and settings.set of either once credential_policy exists is refused with 'Set it under Claude: which to use first.'; POST /settings/billing-order keeps working and writes the policy with the order changed. Open budget cards with source 'plan' filed before go on at the new month as today.

11. What does not change: needsOf, capabilitiesOf and code_commands; the order of rows within a kind; a subscription never used for another person's agent; an API key never through Claude Code; the hooks and the sandbox (the caps port gains the key-monthly level beside 'plan', nothing else); the refused-credential fingerprint; ADR 0112's pause at a money limit; the monthly cap of all spending and the project budget; whether a session continues after a wait and its after-the-wait words (the starts design).
alternatives_rejected: A separate rule per kind of stop (limit, plan share, key limit, refusal): the owner said a refusal follows the same framework 'as if it has run out'; more knobs make more combinations to get wrong and to test; one rule, and the refusal also tells.

A separate rule per kind of call (tasks wait, chat and reviews move, today's ADR 0100 point 4): exactly what 7b rejects ('should definitely not automatically do something even when told to wait'); a review or a plan on the API key while its task waits spends the money the person said to save.

A per-project policy: doubles every path, card and test, and the wake, the grant and chat would each need to know which applies; the owner asked for one framework the system just follows; a project override can read the same type later if asked for.

One ask card per task or per project: the stop is the credential's; N cards for one event are noise and invite answers that disagree; one card per credential stop, covering every call that waits on it.

Keeping the session alive while it asks: one active session per agent would block every other project's work for hours; the session ends with a wait entry naming it and the answer continues it (D6's continuation), so nothing runs that the person did not start.
A grant that lasts until changed ('always use my API key from now on'): that is preset A; a grant for this stop only keeps 'ask' meaning ask at the next stop.
A free order editor for many credentials: a person has at most one subscription and one API key per install; six presets cover every combination and read as sentences with the order visible.
Retrying a refused credential after a while: Anthropic's refusal is final for that credential and repeated attempts risk locking the account; only a different credential (its fingerprint) ends it.

Moving a task to a credential that can do less at a stop under 'next' (today's groups loop): the owner's rule of 2026-11-02, 'another credential only when the first cannot do the task properly'; waiting and saying why is honest, running the research without pages is not.

Treating the monthly cap of all spending as a stop that switches credentials: subscription spend counts against it as its API-equivalent, so no switch can help; it stays ADR 0112's pause with its card.
Rewriting the stored settings once at start (a data migration): a read-time mapping changes nothing for anyone, is restart-safe by construction, and keeps old Undo rows meaningful.

Filing an Inbox card when chat alone meets a held credential: the person is in the chat; a per-turn button is the smallest consent and spends nothing until pressed; the card is filed only when work waits.

A per-turn 'are you sure' on every switch under 'next': that is 'ask'; 'next' is the person's chosen 'and then the system just does it', made transparent by the lines, the result, Costs and one notification.

Letting the per-call caps ignore the key's own monthly limit (checked only at pick, as today's limits.monthlyUsdMicro is): a run in progress would pass it; the owner's rule is that no cap is ever passed.

decisions: CP-1 One policy type in the billing package (credential_policy { order, whenStopped: next | ask | wait, keyMonthlyUsdMicro? }), read at every pick from notify_prefs with a read-time mapping of the two old settings. Why: the owner's 'a framework for what to use when, and then the system just does it'; reading at every pick makes a Settings change apply to the next call, and the mapping changes nothing a person chose.

CP-2 The router's 'held' list covers every stop (resting, refused, plan_share, monthly_cap), each with its until and a stop key; ctx.whenStopped replaces waitOnRest; under 'ask' and 'wait' a held first choice throws the wait unless a grant for that exact stop key names the credential that would serve; 'next' moves as today. Why: 7a/7b/7c, and one place decides so every caller agrees.

CP-3 RouterTaskBilling passes the person's rule for every purpose (tasks, critic, interactive, chat, batch) and never moves to a lower chooser group at a stop (the task waits with reason 'needs'); the key's monthly limit from the policy is applied to the API key's source as limits.monthlyUsdMicro in the router's view (no row write). Why: one rule for every call (lens), and 'properly' (2026-11-02).

CP-4 RoutedProvider follows the rule: after it rests or marks a source it picks again under the rule; under 'ask' and 'wait' the call ends with the wait (code unavailable, details.wait) and its caller handles it (the critic: the review waits; planning: the plan waits; chat: the hold reply; batch: skip); under 'next' one move as today, recorded with its cost. Why: D5-1 is the main money leak today.

CP-5 Task runs under 'ask': the stopped task and every task whose first choice it is wait like under 'wait', and one ask card is ensured for the stop; under 'next' the stopped task re-runs on the next credential in the session from its kept work, recorded as billing.switch. Why: 7a ('completed by the API ... transparent') and 'ask first' as one card.

CP-6 A credential's cap reached mid-run follows the rule: the plan-share level (no budget card for a new stop; next: continues on the other credential from its kept work; ask: the card; wait: waits until the share has room, at the new month or a raised allowance) and a new key-monthly cap level checked before each call beside 'plan'. Old open 'plan' budget cards keep going on at the new month. Why: 7a and 'no cap is ever passed'; a raised allowance must end the wait (nothing stuck silently).

CP-7 The ask card: filed only by the writer that set limits.asking for the stop key (version-checked); answered once; 'use' re-reads the stop, writes the grant (version-checked, audit billing.grant), closes the card and starts the waiting session's continuation as a person start (the starts design's API) or drafts the waiting plan again; 'wait' closes it and moves nothing; a late or second answer changes nothing and returns the card's Done line; the wake withdraws it (not_needed) when its stop ends or the policy changes, and ends grants whose stop is over. Why: answered once, late answers handled, restart-safe.

CP-8 A refusal files one card behind its mark (concurrent refusals file one), carries the choice under 'ask', moves the work under 'next', and a refused credential gets no second request from any path until a different credential is saved. Why: 7c and the account-lock rule.

CP-9 Chat asks the routed provider whether its call is held before the model path; held: no model call, the hold reply with a per-turn 'Use API key' (the person's press lets that one call switch: allowSwitch on that request only); under 'next' the footer names the credential and the CHF. Why: chat spends too; the smallest consent.

CP-10 Background jobs (batch: the model watch, its evals; the monthly calibration) never ask and never switch under 'ask' or 'wait'; held, the run spends nothing, logs one line and is not marked done for its period. Why: no card for work nobody started; no silent money.

CP-11 Under 'next' one notification per switch event and session (deduplicated by limits.switchNotified { stopKey, sessionId }, restart-safe); none for a wait. Why: 7c 'notification or information'; D6 'no reminders' for waiting work.

CP-12 Switch data: the run row records why it ran where it did (artifact switchedFrom { kind, stop }), the session log gets billing.switch and billing.back events, the SessionResult gets switched [{ taskId, from, to, usdMicro }] summed from the ledger; RoutedProvider's fallback sentence uses the person's clock. Why: every screen's words (d1109-cred-words) read data, not re-parsed sentences.

CP-13 settings.set credential_policy: risk by direction (narrowing acts at once; widening needs the person's yes; an agent actor cannot widen; an Undo is judged the same way); the legacy keys are hidden from the chat model's settings tool and refused once the policy exists; an old billing_order or mid_session_limit change-log row's Undo is blocked with a sentence once credential_policy exists. Why: money settings never widen by text; the tool description is model-facing code.
root_causes: The 'wait' rule is a flag the executor sets on task-run picks (waitOnRest), not a property of the person's policy that every pick reads; RoutedProvider's one-time move to the next source is unconditional.
BillingRouter's held list knows only resting and refused sources; plan_share and monthly_limit are plain skips.
The plan-share cap reached mid-run is handled as a money budget level (ADR 0112's pause, a budget card that waits for the month), on a separate path from credential stops, and never reads the rule.
There is no state for 'asked' or 'granted': a decision the person makes about a stop has nowhere to live, so only two automatic outcomes exist.
RouterTaskBilling's groups loop moves down a chooser group on any 'no source' that is not a hold.
Switch facts exist only as words (a log sentence and an audit row), not as data on the run, the session event and the result, so no screen can show a switch with its cost.
Filing a credential card is not tied to the version-checked mark that decided it (every caller files), so concurrent stops can file twice.
The key's own monthly limit has no per-call cap level and no writer.

decisions: CW-1 One Settings section in Basics, 'Claude: which to use first, and when it runs out', replacing the Move up / Move down part of BillingOrderSection and the mid_session_limit row: the credentials in order with what each costs, six presets as label and line, the 'runs out means' line, the one-credential and the not-chosen states; widening asks once with the money sentence. CW-2 The API key's monthly limit as an optional CHF field in the same section, stored in the policy (USD); narrowing at once, raising or clearing a yes; 0 refused in words. Why: it makes 'API key first, then subscription' meaningful and the limit is a stop the engine enforces.

CW-3 The ask card's words are computed when shown (the estimate, the reset time in the person's zone, whether the other credential can serve, the caps' room), one card per stop, buttons of at most three words ('Use API key', 'Use subscription', 'Wait until 15:40'), consequence lines under 100 characters, Done lines for every outcome. Why: design §3.8 and §5, the true-now rule.
CW-4 The refused card's body follows the rule and never promises a start by itself unless a session waits to go on (then the starts design's words). Why: 7c and D6.
CW-5 The Start dialog's and the plan card's line from one function ifRunsOutLine(policy, saved kinds); none with one credential. Why: the person knows before Start what the system will do.
CW-6 Task rows and the drawer name each stop and the ask, and a switched run with the CHF the ledger booked. Why: transparency on the task (7a).
CW-7 The project status: rule 1 gains the ask ('Waiting for you: use your API key?'); the waiting line names the plan share and the key limit. Why: design §2, one sentence.
CW-8 The session page's lines for billing.switch and billing.back, and the result's switched line with the ledger's CHF. Why: transparency on the session (7a).
CW-9 Costs gains 'By credential'. Why: the spend shows the switch (7a).

CW-10 Under 'wait' (and 'ask' before an answer) the Start dialog offers 'Start on API key' when the first choice is stopped and the other can serve: a grant for this stop plus a person start. Why: 'wait' means the app does nothing by itself, not that the person cannot choose; the press is the person's.

adr: Next free number (0120 if the run C designs take 0114 to 0119; the session lead renumbers) — One credential policy: the person's order and one rule for when a credential stops (go on with the next one by itself, ask first, or wait), followed by every model call (task runs, the critic's reviews, planning, chat, the task check, background jobs). A stop is a usage limit, the plan-share cap, the API key's own monthly limit or a refusal; the monthly cap of all spending and the budgets are no stop and are never passed by a switch. Under 'wait' nothing moves onto another credential in either direction; under 'ask' one Inbox card per stop offers the other credential with its cost and the reset time, and its yes is a grant for that stop only, which continues the waiting session as the person's start; under 'next' the work goes on at once, the stopped task too from its kept work, never onto a credential that cannot do it as properly. A refusal follows the same rule, always files its card, and the refused credential is never called again until a different one is saved. Every switch is recorded on the run, the session and the ledger and shown with its CHF; under 'next' one notification per switch. Stored as human.notify_prefs.credential_policy; the old billing_order and mid_session_limit are read as the policy until the person chooses. Amends ADR 0100 (points 2, 4, 10 and 15, and the amendments' 'Wait'), 0044 (the plan-share cap is a stop), 0098 (CALL_FALLBACK_ORDER only for a person who never chose), 0107 (a stop never moves a task down the chooser's groups), 0112 (a pause at the subscription's share follows the policy; the caps gain the key's monthly level).
